rationale: Across the provided literature, YWHAZ-related neurodevelopmental disorder (Popov-Chang syndrome, OMIM #618428) is characterized by global developmental delay, intellectual disability, dysmorphic facial features, seizures, non-specific brain malformations, and variable cardiac anomalies. In contrast, severe classic lissencephaly (grade 1-3 agyria/pachygyria) and limb reduction defects are not reported in YWHAZ cohorts and remain categorized with distinct genetic etiologies (such as PAFAH1B1/YWHAE in Miller-Dieker syndrome and isolated lissencephaly), confirming their utility as negative discriminating features.

evidence.text: Variants in YWHAZ cause intellectual disability, global developmental delay, and brain malformation with cognitive defects, distinguishing its pathology from classic lissencephaly syndromes.

new_directions.question_text: What specific neuroimaging criteria reliably differentiate YWHAZ-associated brain malformations from mild posterior pachygyria observed in atypical 17p13.3 microdeletions?
new_directions.rationale: Clarifying the exact radiological boundaries of brain malformations in YWHAZ will ensure that subtle cortical organization defects are not misclassified as mild pachygyria.

new_directions.question_text: What is the true prevalence and spectrum of cardiac septal and conotruncal defects across all genetically confirmed YWHAZ missense and loss-of-function variants?
new_directions.rationale: Quantifying the penetrance of cardiac anomalies will refine whether congenital heart defects can serve as a secondary discriminator when cortical imaging is non-diagnostic.
